content:
Let \(M=(a,a+\frac4a)\), \(a>0\).

The line through \(M\) perpendicular to \(y=x\) has slope \(-1\):
\[
y-\left(a+\frac4a\right)=-(x-a).
\]
Solving with \(y=x\):
\[
x=2a+\frac4a-x \implies x=a+\frac2a,
\]
so
\[
A=\left(a+\frac2a,\ a+\frac2a\right).
\]
Thus
\[
\overrightarrow{MA}=\left(\frac2a,-\frac2a\right).
\]
The foot \(B\) on the \(y\)-axis is
\[
B=\left(0,a+\frac4a\right),
\]
so
\[
\overrightarrow{MB}=(-a,0).
\]
Therefore,
\[
\overrightarrow{MA}\cdot\overrightarrow{MB}
=\left(\frac2a\right)(-a)+\left(-\frac2a\right)(0)
=-2.
\]

\[
\boxed{-2}
\]
